messages:
ella: Hey team — copy pass for the "Apply quantization" confirmation modal. This shows when a customer chooses to apply a quantization profile to a model version. Goal: clear about irreversible perf/quality tradeoffs, avoid scaring beginners, and surface rollback path. Drafts below.

ella: Draft 1 (explicit risk):
`Apply quantization to model-v2? This may reduce output quality but will lower inference cost and latency. This operation is reversible but may require redeploying. Continue \u00b7 Cancel`

ella: Draft 2 (reassuring):
`Apply quantization profile to model-v2. This can reduce cost and latency; you may notice small quality differences. We save a rollback snapshot. Apply \u00b7 Cancel`

ella: Draft 3 (action-first):
`Ready to apply quantization? Save a snapshot so you can revert later. Apply now \u00b7 Cancel`

fran: Product: I like 2 for tone. But "small" is vague. Use "minor" or "subtle"? Also call out that metrics may change for evals. Maybe add a one-line note: "Quality regressions are possible; run your eval suite after applying."

tom: Infra: avoid saying "irreversible" if rollback is possible but takes time. Suggest: "The change can be reverted, but reverting may require redeploying the model."

aria: UX: keep primary CTA clear. Use verbs that map to actions: `Apply quantization` instead of just `Apply`. Secondary should be `Cancel`. For extra safety add a checkbox: "I understand this may affect output quality" before enabling Apply. But be careful for accessibility — label must be explicit.

ella: Good. Localization note: avoid embedding model ids in sentences (model-v2) — translators prefer placeholders: `{{model_name}}`. We'll use keys.

fran: Metrics callout idea: inline link to `Run eval suite` and note: `recommended after applying`. So small inline sentence: `We recommend running your eval suite to check for regressions.` Link `run eval suite` to the eval page.

tom: Also include an opt-in telemetry flag for quantization experiments: `telemetry.quant.apply=true` so we can A/B measure impact on latency/cost.

aria: Accessibility: confirm modal has role=dialog, focus trap, and the checkbox is keyboard accessible. If we add the warning checkbox, make sure screen readers announce the extra requirement. Also the cancel button should be first to avoid accidental confirmation on Enter. But platform convention usually puts primary on the right. Consider pattern consistency.

ella: Proposed final copy (uses placeholders):
`Apply quantization profile to {{model_name}}? This can reduce inference cost and latency. You may notice minor output quality differences. We recommend running your eval suite to check for regressions.

[ ] I understand this may affect output quality

Cancel \u00b7 Apply quantization`

fran: Suggestion: move the recommendation sentence under the checkbox so it's visible but separate. Also change checkbox text to: `I understand this may change output quality and evaluation metrics.` More precise.

tom: Add tooltip on Apply quantization (on hover/focus): `Applying quantization will change model weights and may change outputs. A rollback snapshot is stored but redeployment may be required.` Keep tooltip concise.

aria: For keyboard users, the checkbox being required could be annoying; consider making it optional but show a stronger visual affordance and require confirmation only for high-risk profiles (e.g., int8 aggressive). We should add variable copy depending on risk level.

ella: Good call. Let's create three severity levels: low/mild/high with slightly different copy. Draft snippets:
- low: `This profile reduces cost with minimal expected quality impact.`
- mild: `This profile reduces cost and may cause minor quality differences. Test with your eval suite.`
- high: `This profile may materially affect output quality. We strongly recommend running your eval suite and creating a rollback snapshot.`

fran: Nice. Add translation keys per sentence: `quant.modal.title`, `quant.modal.body.low`, `.mild`, `.high`, `quant.modal.checkbox`, `quant.modal.apply_cta`. Intl-bot: please confirm char limits for some languages.

intl-bot: Reminder: keep English sentence length under 140 chars where feasible. Provide context strings for placeholders. Also include a short key for tooltip: `quant.modal.tooltip`.

elia: (typo, meant ella) Updated final proposal for PR:
- Title: `Apply quantization profile`
- Body (mild): `Applying this profile can lower inference cost and latency. You may notice minor output quality differences. We recommend running your eval suite after applying.`
- Checkbox: `I understand this may change output quality and evaluation metrics.`
- Buttons: `Cancel` (secondary), `Apply quantization` (primary)
- Tooltip (on Apply): `Saves a rollback snapshot and updates model binaries. Reverting may require redeploying the model.`

fran: LGTM. QA note: include an integration test that ensures the checkbox text appears for mild/high profiles, tooltip exists, and CTA is disabled until checkbox checked for high severity.

tom: Engineering note: include machine flag `quant.apply_request=true` in the payload and `quant.risk_level=low|mild|high` so SDKs can render appropriate copy. Also ensure we don't expose internal profile ids in UI strings.

aria: Accessibility checklist: role=dialog, aria-labelledby for title, aria-describedby for body, checkbox labelled, focus on checkbox or cancel, ensure tooltip accessible via keyboard and announced on reveal.

ella: I'll update the Figma modal, add translation key table, and create the PR with the three risk variants. Thanks all!"
